answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits catch fabricated work. A Sybil attacker must therefore tie up real capital for every fake account, rather than minting identities for free; splitting one stake across a comet, crystal, and mirror of accounts does not multiply voting weight. Audits and delayed withdrawals make the attack costly even if some fakes pass at first.
